text:
maya: Quick heads-up — dashboards are showing a delta in route latency and token-metering between v1 and v2 for a small subset of tenants (cohort_id=shadow-A). Anyone else seeing this?
liam: saw it earlier, might be batching differences. what's the delta?
maya: v1 median p95 ~ 120ms, v2 p95 ~ 210ms for short completions (<100 tokens). Token count accounting shows ~12% higher per-token tally on v2 for same requests.
cheng: can you paste the console query / timeline? Might be aggregation mismatch (per-route vs per-variant).
maya: pasted snapshot from console:
```sql
SELECT route, variant, p95_latency_ms, tokens FROM metrics WHERE cohort='shadow-A' AND ts>now()-1h
```
maya: result snippet: v1 p95 118ms tokens 9.8k; v2 p95 212ms tokens 11.0k
hailey: do we know if v2 is hitting a different model variant/quanta config? v2 sometimes uses micro-batching by default.
liam: micro-batching would increase tail for small seq lengths. Also could be kv-cache eviction differences.
maya: @liam @cheng can we check routing logs? I'm seeing a mix of base-v2 and base-v2-quantized fallbacks in the same minute.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: 1 new rollout event: console.flag.v2_rollout toggle=on for tenant shadow-A at 2025-03-05T14:02:10Z
cheng: rollouts were toggled for that cohort earlier today. If fallback pairs are different capacity classes, smart-routing could prefer cheaper variant, causing small request latency differences.
hailey: telemetry note: billing pipeline deduped tokens differently for v2 for a month due to header change (x-variant -> x-model-variant). Could explain accounting bump.
maya: good catch. That still doesn't explain p95 doubling. Any ideas for probe setup?
liam: propose a 2-hour A/B with pinned routing (force v1 vs force v2) on the same hardware pool to isolate runtime differences. Also capture per-request kernel path and batch size.
maya: agreed. can we add a console panel for "batch-size distribution" and "kernel-path tag"? ideally as a temporary debug widget.
cheng: we have kernel_path logged in trace metadata. I'll make a temp panel and wire a chart by cohort and variant.
hailey: add a quick eval: run 300 synthetic requests (seq len 10-50) to both variants from the same client and collect latency + tokens. I'll run after the panel exists.
maya: if the issue is kv-eviction we should be able to reproduce by repeating prompts with increasing seqlen and checking cache-hit header.
liam: also worth checking fallthrough routing: if v2 is configured to fall back to quantized when load > 70% that could explain sporadic tail.
maya: can someone check capacity telemetry for the pool at 14:00-14:10? I saw small scale event in autoscaler logs around 14:03.
ops-bot: autoscaler-bot: scale-event pool=gpu-pool-3 old=6 new=8 at 2025-03-05T14:03:05Z reason=CPU_pressure
cheng: autoscale happened — if new nodes joined mid-window batching semantics change temporarily.
maya: plan: cheng to add panel + routing-log filter, liam to run pinned A/B with client harness, hailey to run synthetic eval, maya to collect results and post back. I'll also add a telemetry alert if v2 p95 exceeds v1 by >50% for 10m.
liam: FYI I added a short-run script in infra/smoke-tests to force kernel debug headers: `./run_small_latency_check.sh --variant base-v2 --tag kernel-path`
hailey: noted. tagging @product for rollout UX feedback — big p95 deltas will trigger alerts for customers.
product-bot: product-notify: prod-team: heads up — engineers are investigating variant p95 delta; may impact rollout cadence.
maya: thanks all. will report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
